answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity pay its own way: before a vote or task counts, the agent must lock a bond in a shared vault. Picture a jetty built from paid stones, where every fake voice must bring a stone of its own, so an attacker wanting a thousand identities pays a thousand bonds, not one. If peers later prove an identity was forged, its bond is slashed. That converts a free lie into a bill: the ridge between honest and fake agents is made of collateral, and the fable that names are cheap collapses once every name carries a price.
